title: Alchemy, and the systems around it
eyebrow: INDEPENDENT ENGINEERING / THE PUBLIC HOME OF ALCHEMY
headline: Systems that understand intention.
intro: Software is more than its code. It has to know what is being asked, who has authority, and what must endure.
summary: Alchemy is a connected body of work in intelligence, perception, communication, secure protocols and distributed software. Rasen Falcon is where that work becomes accessible.

sections.heading: A different kind of software architecture
sections.body: Alchemy brings together independently usable services: each has a defined responsibility, a language-neutral boundary where appropriate, and an explicit account of state and authority. The purpose is composition without forcing every application through a single framework.

sections.heading: Perception, made useful
sections.body: Signals, sound, image, moving pictures and three-dimensional worlds are different media, but the questions we ask of them often have the same structure: what is present, what changed, and what can we support with evidence?

sections.heading: Intelligence with boundaries
sections.body: An intelligent system should distinguish an intention from an instruction, a suggestion from an authorised action, and a plausible answer from a verified fact. That distinction runs through the Alchemy work.
